_national.labelling: Wine of Origin (WO) scheme under the Liquor Products Act, run by the Wine and Spirit Board: a wine of origin must come 100% from the named unit (geographical unit such as Western Cape; region such as Coastal Region; district such as Stellenbosch; ward such as Simonsberg-Stellenbosch), with narrow exceptions (sweetening up to 5% of natural wine, fortifying spirit). Wine blended from several units needs prescribed approvals (s. 9(3)). Cultivar 85% (since 2006); vintage 85%. Every certified wine is tasted, analysed and sealed. Estate wine: grown, made and bottled on one registered estate unit of contiguous land farmed as a single unit. Single vineyard: a registered block of at most 6 ha; since the 2025 amendments it may be a field blend of white or of red varieties picked, crushed and fermented together; a new "single vine" category also exists. The certified label must show the origin with "Wine of Origin" or "W.O." at least once.
_national.sweetness: Extra dry up to 2.5 g/l; dry up to 5 (or 9 if acidity is within 2 g/l of sugar); semi-dry 5 to 12 (or 18 with acid within 10); semi-sweet 5 to 30. Late harvest at least 20 g/l and 10% abv; Special Late Harvest from must of at least 22 Balling, 11% abv, no concentration, sweetening or spirit, certified; Noble Late Harvest from must of at least 28 Balling, over 50 g/l, sugar-free extract 30 g/l, VA max 1.8 g/l, certified; Wine from naturally dried grapes (straw wine) at least 28 Balling and 16% total alcohol. Sparkling: brut nature under 3 g/l (traditional method only), extra brut under 6, brut under 12, extra dry 12 to 17, dry 17 to 32, semi-sweet 32 to 50, sweet over 50.
_national.styles: Méthode Cap Classique (MCC, separate class from the 2023 harvest): whole-bunch pressed, second fermentation in the bottle sold, at least 12 months on lees (9 for 2022 and earlier), WO certified. MCC with Extended Lees Aging: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and/or Pinot Meunier only, at least 36 months on lees. Plain traditional-method sparkling: 9 months on lees, may not use "MCC". Other legal classes include skin-macerated white (96 hours on skins, under 4 g/l), extended barrel-aged white (2 years in oak), natural pale (2 years under flor, unfortified), méthode ancestrale, Cape white, ruby, tawny, LBV (at least 3 years, 2 in oak) and Cape vintage (at least 1 year in cask or tank), plus fino, amontillado, oloroso and cream classes (3 years in cask, solera rules).
_national.other: Certified Heritage Vineyards seal (Old Vine Project, from 2018): vineyards 35 years or older, with the planting year on the seal. Cape Winemakers Guild (founded 1982, first auction 1985): an invitation-only group of members (42 in 2025) who make small lots sold only at its annual auction. From 31 December 2027 the class designation must also appear on the main label.
